name: Pontus Alv
titles: Founded Polar Skate Co in Malmo, 2011
Founded Last Resort AB footwear
Filmmaker behind Polar's videos, incl. In Search of the Miraculous (2010)
summary: Swedish pro skater, filmmaker and artist who founded Polar Skate Co in Malmo in 2011 and turned DIY spot-building and hand-drawn graphics into an aesthetic the whole industry copied.

name: Mark Appleyard
titles: Thrasher Skater of the Year 2003
Parts in Flip's Sorry (2002) and Really Sorry (2003)
Part in Alien Workshop's Photosynthesis (2000)
Part in Transworld's Modus Operandi (2000)
Part in Globe's United by Fate (2007)
summary: Canadian street skater whose effortless, fast-footed video parts in Photosynthesis and Flip's Sorry made him Thrasher's Skater of the Year in 2003.
photoCredit: Photo: Me, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Jake Brown
titles: X Games Big Air gold 2009 and 2010
X Games Big Air silver 2006 and 2007
Survived a 45-foot fall in the X Games 13 Big Air final, 2007
First to spin a 720 on the MegaRamp without grabbing the board
summary: Australian MegaRamp specialist remembered for the 45-foot slam at X Games 13 in 2007 - and for coming back to win Big Air gold in 2009 and 2010.
photoCredit: Photo: Philkon Phil Konstantin, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Sakura Yosozumi
titles: Olympic park gold, Tokyo 2020
World Park champion 2018 (Nanjing)
Asian Games park gold, Jakarta 2018
X Games park gold, Chiba 2022
summary: Japanese park rider who won the first ever Olympic women's park gold at Tokyo 2020, having already taken the first Asian Games park title in 2018.
photoCredit: Photo: RuinDig/Yuki Uchida, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Kokona Hiraki
titles: Olympic park silver, Tokyo 2020, aged 12
Olympic park silver, Paris 2024
Youngest X Games medalist ever (park silver, Minneapolis 2019)
Vans Park Series Paris winner 2019
summary: Hokkaido park skater who took silver at Tokyo 2020 aged 12 as Japan's youngest ever Olympian, then backed it up with a second park silver in Paris.
photoCredit: Photo: Andy Miah, CC BY-NC 2.0, via Flickr

name: Elliot Sloan
hometown: New York City, New York, USA
titles: 16 X Games medals, 7 gold
X Games Big Air gold, Los Angeles 2013
X Games Big Air gold, Minneapolis 2019
X Games vert best trick gold, Japan 2023
Nitro World Games skateboard best trick gold 2016 and 2017
summary: New York-born MegaRamp and vert skater with 16 X Games medals, including Big Air golds in 2013 and 2019.
photoCredit: Photo: Alex Carvalho, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Andy Macdonald
titles: 8 X Games golds, incl. six straight vert doubles titles with Tony Hawk (1997-2002)
8x World Cup Skateboarding champion
Record for most X Games medals in vert skateboarding (as of 2013)
Oldest Olympic skateboarder ever - Paris 2024 for Great Britain, aged 51
summary: Massachusetts vert veteran, Tony Hawk's long-time doubles partner, who qualified for Paris 2024 for Great Britain at 51 to become the oldest Olympic skateboarder.
photoCredit: Photo: Phil Konstantin, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Pierre-Luc Gagnon
titles: 19 X Games medals, 9 gold (vert, vert doubles, big air, vert best trick)
2x Maloof Money Cup vert winner
Dew Tour and Gravity Games winner
AST China Invitational vert winner, Beijing 2008
summary: Quebec vert skater known as PLG, one of the most decorated ramp riders in X Games history with nine golds among nineteen medals.
photoCredit: Photo: Philkon Phil Konstantin, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Lizzie Armanto
titles: X Games gold in the first women's park event, Barcelona 2013
World Cup of Skateboarding points champion 2010, 2011 and 2012
First woman to complete Tony Hawk's Loop, 2018
Nitro World Games gold 2018
Represented Finland in park at Tokyo 2020
summary: American-Finnish bowl and park rider on the Birdhouse team, winner of the first women's X Games park contest and the first woman to ride Tony Hawk's Loop.
photoCredit: Photo: Stig Nygaard, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Bastien Salabanzi
titles: Tampa Pro winner 2004
X Games street bronze 2004
Copenhagen Pro winner 2007
Globe World Skateboarding Championships (Dortmund) winner 2001, 2002 and 2003
summary: French street prodigy who won the Dortmund World Cup at 15 and took Tampa Pro in 2004, famous for enormous flip tricks down stairs.

name: Chloe Covell
hometown: Tweed Heads, New South Wales, Australia
titles: Youngest X Games gold medallist, street, 2023, aged 13
Six X Games golds (2023 California, 2024 Chiba, 2025 Osaka, 2025 Salt Lake City street and best trick, 2026 Chiba)
World Championship street silver, Sharjah 2022
Competed in women's street at Paris 2024
summary: Australian street skater who became the youngest X Games gold medallist at 13 in 2023 and has piled up X Games titles ever since.

name: Mariah Duran
titles: X Games street gold, Minneapolis 2018
X Games street gold, Sydney 2018
X Games street silver, Austin 2016
World Championship street bronze, Los Angeles 2017
Olympian in street at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024
summary: Goofy-footed street skater from Albuquerque, a double X Games gold medallist in 2018 and a two-time US Olympian.

name: Luan Oliveira
hometown: Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
titles: Tampa Pro winner 2013 and 2015
SLS tour stop wins in Los Angeles and Newark, 2015
World Championship street bronze 2013 and 2015
X Games street silver 2011, 2014 and 2019
Battle at the Berrics winner 2018
summary: Brazilian street skater with famously clean flip tricks, a two-time Tampa Pro champion and one of the most influential skaters of his generation in Brazil.
photoCredit: Photo: Pablo Vaz, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Dashawn Jordan
titles: X Games street gold 2021
X Games street silver, Shanghai 2019
X Games street best trick silver 2021
X Games street best trick bronze 2022
summary: Arizona street skater known for hyper-technical laser flip variations, an X Games street gold medallist in 2021.

name: Sora Shirai
titles: World street champion, Tokyo 2023
X Games street gold, Chiba 2024
World Championship street bronze 2021 (Rome) and 2025 (Sao Paulo)
Olympian in street at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024
Part in Blind's Time Change, 2019
summary: Goofy-footed Kanagawa street skater who won the 2023 street world championship at home in Tokyo and took X Games gold in Chiba the following year.
photoCredit: Photo: RuinDig/Yuki Uchida, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

name: Miyu Ito
titles: Three X Games golds (Ventura 2024 street; Sacramento 2026 street and best trick)
First rookie to win X Games women's street gold, 2024
World Championship street bronze, Rome 2024
Asian Games street bronze, Hangzhou 2022
Japanese national street champion 2022
summary: Yamagata street skater and former snowboarder who won X Games street gold on debut in 2024 and has since added two more golds.
photoCredit: Photo: Skreeen, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
